title: Dominic and the Tryouts
premise: Seventeen-year-old Noor Dravenmoor has perfected the art of being unseen: he cooks, cleans, and covers for his younger siblings while their mother works hospital night shifts, and his one escape is the school's elite a cappella group, where he auditions anonymously each year and never makes callbacks. When his college application demands an essay answering 'What truth have you never said out loud?', Noor writes about the secret singing lessons his late father paid for—and how his best friend Marcus's family, not his own, quietly covered the funeral costs. As the final audition approaches, Noor must choose between protecting Marcus from a betrayal that would shatter their friendship and finally claiming a voice of his own; in the end, he sings the truth itself at tryouts, loses Marcus temporarily, but wins a place in the group and, more importantly, learns that being seen is worth the cost.
about_author: Kestrel Yarrow is a former high school choir accompanist who grew up translating parent-teacher conferences for her own family. She writes stories about kids who carry more than their backpacks suggest.

chapters.title: The Locker Rule
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet the Dravenmoor household at 5:47 a.m.: burnt toast, sibling chaos, mom's night-shift exhaustion. At school, Noor executes his invisibility routine flawlessly. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. English class receives the college essay prompt: 'What truth have you never said out loud?' Noor freezes while classmates joke through it. That night he starts a draft he immediately hides. Beat: the crack in the wall of silence.

chapters.title: Harmony Hallway
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, already in the a cappella group, drags Noor past the music room where tryout flyers hang. Marcus assumes Noor isn't interested; Noor lets him believe it. Beat: friendship built on Noor's convenient silences.

chapters.title: What Dad Left
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Cleaning out a closet, Noor finds receipts for voice lessons his father secretly arranged before dying—paid by checks signed by Marcus's father. The inheritance isn't money; it's an unspoken debt. Beat: vertigo of gratitude entangled with shame.

chapters.title: Draft One, Deleted
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor writes the essay honestly—the funeral, the checks, the lessons—then deletes it, terrified of what telling Marcus would mean. His sister Zoya catches him crying and pretends she didn't. Beat: the cost of honesty made concrete.

chapters.title: Anonymous Auditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tryouts open with blind auditions behind a screen. Noor signs up under a false name, his first act of open rebellion. He sings; the room goes still. Beat: exhilaration of being heard without being seen.

chapters.title: Callback List
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus reads the callback list and sees 'N. Draven'—and recognizes the voice instantly. He says nothing to Noor, unsettled. Beat: loyalty beginning to strain against suspicion.

chapters.title: Mom's Double Shifts
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Mom picks up extra shifts to cover Zoya's field trip fees; Noor cancels his own plans again without complaint. The callback rehearsal conflicts with pickup duty. Beat: the invisible labor no one grades.

chapters.title: The Arrangement
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor negotiates with Zoya: she covers Tuesdays if he never tells Mom about her broken window. Sibling barter as love language. He commits to callbacks. Beat: fragile infrastructure holding the family up.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Room Ghost
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. At callbacks, Marcus watches 'N. Draven' sing and can't reconcile the voice with his silent best friend. The director praises the mystery auditioner. Beat: admiration curdling into hurt at being kept out.

chapters.title: The Question Behind the Question
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. College counselor Ms. Okafor reads Noor's safe, dishonest draft and asks one question: 'Who are you protecting?' Noor can't answer. Beat: the essay prompt turning inward like a mirror.

chapters.title: Overheard
chapters.summary: Zoya's POV. Zoya overhears Noor practicing and discovers his talent—and then, snooping, finds the old receipts. She confronts him gently: 'You let us think you were ordinary.' Beat: family seeing him truly for the first time.

chapters.title: Marcus's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus asks his dad about the Dravenmoor funeral checks; his father dismisses it as 'what neighbors do.' Marcus realizes Noor has carried this alone for years. Beat: anger at the silence, not the secret.

chapters.title: Rising Tension
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Final audition week. Rumors swirl about the anonymous standout; Marcus grows cold toward Noor without explanation. Noor, sensing it, doubles down on hiding. Beat: two friends orbiting the same unsaid thing.

chapters.title: The Blowup
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus confronts Noor: 'I've been cheering for someone who doesn't exist.' Noor deflects; Marcus walks. The friendship cracks along the exact fault line of the essay prompt. Beat: the cost arrives early.

chapters.title: Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Mom, awake at dawn, finds Noor staring at nothing. She tells him about the nights she almost quit, and that his father sang to her in the hospital hallway once. Beat: inherited courage passed down.

chapters.title: Rewrite
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor rewrites the essay in one sitting—true, specific, unflinching—including Marcus's name. He submits it before he can flinch. Beat: the point of no return on paper.

chapters.title: Final Audition Eve
chapters.summary: Zoya's POV. The siblings stage an intervention of snacks and blunt advice. Zoya tells him to sing the truth, not just a song. Noor decides what he'll do tomorrow. Beat: the family as chorus.

chapters.title: The Audition
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Onstage before the whole school, Noor removes the anonymity screen himself, introduces himself, and sings—then speaks the truth about the lessons, the debt, and Marcus aloud. Silence, then applause. Beat: climax; visibility chosen, not forced.

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus doesn't come to him after. Days pass. Noor endures the school's attention and the group's offer of a spot, hollow without his friend. Beat: victory with a hole in it.

chapters.title: Locker Open
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marcus shows up at Noor's locker with the old lesson receipts taped inside his own: 'Dad kept copies too. I thought I was the only one keeping score.' They don't fix everything—but they start. Beat: reconciliation earned, not gifted.

chapters.title: Ensemble
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. First official rehearsal: Noor takes a harmony part, visible, named. At home, Mom frames his acceptance letter beside Dad's photo. The essay gets him into college; the truth got him here. Beat: resolution—an inheritance finally claimed.
